modules.title: Lesson 1: Understanding Salvation
modules.description: Explore sin, God's redemptive plan, salvation by grace, and the evidence of genuine conversion.
modules.introduction: Salvation is God's work of delivering humanity from sin and restoring relationship with Himself through Jesus Christ. It is not church attendance, moral reform, or family inheritance.

lessons.title: The problem of sin and God's rescue
lessons.content: Sin is rebellion against God and has spiritual and relational consequences. Salvation is God's rescue through Christ, received by grace through faith, not earned by works.

lessons.title: Justification, regeneration, and adoption
lessons.content: In Christ, God declares believers righteous, gives new spiritual life, and welcomes them into His family with access, inheritance, intimacy, and identity.

lessons.title: Assurance and evidence of conversion
lessons.content: Assurance rests on God's promises, Christ's finished work, and the Spirit's witness. Genuine conversion produces new desires, obedience, love for others, and progressive growth. Zacchaeus illustrates changed behavior and restitution.

discussionQuestions: Why is understanding sin important for understanding salvation?
What is the difference between justification and regeneration?
Why can good works never earn salvation?
What practical signs of transformation can a believer identify?
reviewQuestions: Name three biblical evidences of genuine conversion.
assignments: Write a testimony describing life before Christ, how you met Him, and what has changed.
modules.conclusion: Salvation is God's loving rescue through the finished work of Jesus, received by grace through faith and resulting in a transformed life.

modules.title: Lesson 2: What is a Disciple?
modules.description: Move from church attendance to intentionally following Christ and helping others follow Him.
scriptureReferences: Matthew 28:19–20; Luke 6:40; Luke 9:23–25; John 15:1–8; Acts 11:26; 2 Timothy 2:2
modules.introduction: Salvation brings people into God's family; discipleship forms them into Christ's likeness. Jesus commanded His followers to make disciples, not merely gather attendees.

lessons.title: A disciple follows to become like Christ
lessons.content: The Greek word mathetes means learner, student, or apprentice. A disciple intentionally learns from Christ, obeys His Word, and helps others follow Him.

lessons.title: Count the cost and abide in Christ
lessons.content: Jesus calls disciples to deny themselves, take up the cross daily, and follow Him. Abiding in Christ is the source of fruitfulness, prayer, and spiritual vitality.

lessons.title: Multiply through community and commitment
lessons.content: The early church practiced teaching, fellowship, and prayer. Paul described a four-generation pattern of passing truth to faithful people who teach others. Use mentorship, small groups, and accountability to support growth.

discussionQuestions: What distinguishes a disciple from a regular church attendee?
Why did Jesus emphasize the cost of following Him?
Who is discipling you, and whom are you helping to follow Christ?
reviewQuestions: What does the word disciple mean?
Name two practices that help a disciple grow and multiply.
assignments: Write a personal discipleship commitment and identify one person for accountability and one person to encourage.
modules.conclusion: Discipleship is a daily path of learning, obedience, abiding in Christ, and helping others follow Him.

modules.title: Lesson 3: The Lordship of Jesus Christ
modules.description: Understand Christ's authority over every area of a believer's life.
modules.introduction: Many accept Jesus as Savior, but fewer submit to Him as Lord. Salvation brings forgiveness; lordship concerns authority, allegiance, and obedience.

lessons.title: What it means to call Jesus Lord
lessons.content: Lord means master, owner, and sovereign ruler. Confessing Jesus as Lord declares that we belong to Him and submit our will to His authority.

lessons.title: Dimensions of Christ's lordship
lessons.content: Christ's authority shapes the mind, will, body, possessions, and relationships. Partial obedience is still resistance; lordship includes practical surrender in daily decisions.

lessons.title: Practice daily surrender
lessons.content: Begin with surrender in prayer, make decisions through Scripture, obey promptly, invite accountability, and regularly examine motives. Lordship brings direction, peace, and fruitfulness.

discussionQuestions: Why can Jesus not be Savior without being Lord?
Which area of life is hardest to submit to Christ?
How does lordship affect daily decisions?
reviewQuestions: What does the word Lord communicate about Jesus?
Name three areas shaped by Christ's lordship.
assignments: Write down areas of your life and surrender them in prayer; take one step on a delayed act of obedience.
modules.conclusion: The same Jesus who saves is Lord. Surrender to His authority in every area and follow Him in daily obedience.

modules.title: Lesson 4: Repentance, Faith & Identity in Christ
modules.description: Turn from sin, trust Christ, and embrace your new identity in Him.
modules.introduction: Repentance turns a person from sin, faith turns a person toward Christ, and identity in Christ changes how a believer sees themselves and lives.

lessons.title: Repentance and faith
lessons.content: Repentance is a change of mind, heart, and direction, not merely feeling sorry. Saving faith trusts Christ personally and produces obedience. Baptism publicly identifies a believer with Christ but does not earn salvation.

lessons.title: Identity in Christ
lessons.content: Those in Christ are new creations, forgiven, adopted, and no longer defined by condemnation or past failure. Identity transformation is foundational for growth.

lessons.title: Live from a new identity
lessons.content: Reject condemning thoughts, speak Scripture-based truth, obey promptly, and seek accountability. Authority flows from position in Christ, not from emotion or pride.

discussionQuestions: What is the difference between regret and repentance?
Why did Jesus teach people to count the cost of following Him?
How does identity in Christ affect behavior?
reviewQuestions: How do repentance and faith relate to one another?
Name two truths about identity in Christ.
assignments: Write a declaration of who you are in Christ and identify one old label to reject.
modules.conclusion: Repentance changes direction, faith rests in Christ, and a new identity shapes a transformed life.

modules.title: Lesson 5: Assurance of Salvation & The Holy Spirit
modules.description: Build assurance on God's promises and understand the Spirit's presence and work in the believer.
modules.introduction: Assurance is not built on fluctuating feelings. It rests on the promises of God, the finished work of Christ, the Spirit's witness, and the evidence of growth.

lessons.title: Ground assurance in truth
lessons.content: Salvation is a gift of grace received through faith. Evidence includes a growing direction of obedience, love for God and others, sensitivity to sin, and spiritual growth.

lessons.title: The Holy Spirit and the believer
lessons.content: The Spirit indwells believers, bears witness that they belong to God, forms Christlike fruit, and gives gifts for service and edification. Gifts do not replace character.

lessons.title: Walk in the Spirit daily
lessons.content: Daily dependence includes prayer, Scripture, immediate obedience, fellowship, and responding to conviction. Spiritual growth is more than emotional intensity.

discussionQuestions: How can someone know they are genuinely saved?
What is the difference between spiritual fruit and gifts?
What does walking in the Spirit look like in daily life?
reviewQuestions: Name the foundations of assurance in Christ.
How does the Spirit shape a believer's character?
assignments: List evidence of spiritual growth and identify one fruit of the Spirit to cultivate.
modules.conclusion: Assurance rests on God's work, and the Spirit forms believers for a life of character, service, and ongoing growth.

modules.title: Lesson 6: The Word of God
modules.description: Study Scripture carefully and apply it as the foundation for spiritual formation.
modules.introduction: Spiritual growth depends on Scripture. Prayer connects us relationally with God, while the Word anchors believers in truth and equips them for good work.

lessons.title: Inspiration and authority
lessons.content: Scripture is God-breathed and useful for teaching, correction, and training in righteousness. Handle the text carefully and respect context.

lessons.title: Meditation and study
lessons.content: Biblical meditation fills the mind with truth through reading, reflection, repetition, personalization, and prayer. Inductive study observes, interprets, and applies the passage.

lessons.title: Apply and remember the Word
lessons.content: Study should lead to obedience. Ask what the text teaches about God, what it reveals about people, and what command, promise, or warning calls for response. Memorization helps internalize truth.

discussionQuestions: Why is Scripture a final authority for Christian belief and practice?
What is the difference between reading and meditating?
Why is application essential to Bible study?
reviewQuestions: Name the three steps of inductive Bible study.
What questions help you apply a passage?
assignments: Use the observation, interpretation, and application method to study one chapter this week.
modules.conclusion: Engage Scripture consistently, interpret it responsibly, and let understanding lead to practical obedience.
